comment: T-2505. Tests whose failure is tolerated until a stated date. An entry needs a file, the test's FULL title (describe ancestry joined to the test title by ' › '), a reason saying what is actually known about the flake, the ticket that will remove the entry, and an expiry no more than 42 days out. On the day after `expires` the build fails whether or not the test did — an expiry nobody enforces is a disabled test wearing a deadline. internal/e2egate/gate_test.go's TestRepoQuarantineIsValid checks this file on every `make check`, so an entry that quietly expires turns the tree red without anyone running the e2e suite. Empty is the healthy state; keeping it that way is the point.

entries.title: scale-lab (v2 canvas renderer): pan/zoom frame timings at the documented scale target
entries.reason: Times out at 120s if and only if BOTH other tests in its own file ran first. Bisected 2026-08-12 and reproduced 4/4 on an idle machine, INCLUDING on unmodified main with the pre-T-2505 Playwright config: 127+258 passes (33s), 174+258 passes (58s), 127+174+258 fails. Not order-dependent app state — the scale stack's SQLite store holds no layout row after the failing run. Not CPU: the same test alone under taskset -c 0,1 passes in 19.5s. It passed in the 91-test serial suite, so the sharded arrangement did not cause it, only stopped hiding it. UPDATE 2026-08-17 (T-3204): the 'shared browser process' hypothesis this entry implied is REFUTED — reproduced 4/4 running the initial-render, v1 pan/zoom and v2 pan/zoom tests as THREE SEPARATE Playwright invocations (three distinct Chromium processes) against one long-lived vnproxd; a fresh daemon serving v2 alone (nothing preceding it) passes reliably in ~15-32s every time. So the dependency is on the DAEMON'S accumulated wall-clock uptime/request history, not on browser-process reuse. The daemon itself stays healthy throughout the hang (goroutine count flat 49->64 and stable, CPU ~30-33%, RSS ~63-71MB via VNPROX_DEBUG_PPROF_ADDR sampling every 3s) — server-side resource exhaustion (goroutine leak, CPU spin, memory growth) is ruled out. Playwright's own trace shows the failure is not a cascade of retries: a single `page.mouse.move()` CDP call, issued ~12s into the test during the first pan gesture's second pass, simply never returns for the remaining ~110s until the 120s test timeout fires — i.e. the browser's input dispatch/renderer wedges on one call, once the daemon is old enough. Candidate mechanism not yet confirmed: internal/api/topology.go's `staleConsecutiveFailures` (peer hosts read as permanently unreachable in this fixture) and/or TopologyCanvasV2's synchronous per-viewport-change canvas redraw (drawScene, gated by `hasDriftEntity`'s setInterval pulse) doing more work once more entities carry non-default badges — V1 (react-flow) has no equivalent synchronous full-redraw-per-mousemove path and never reproduces this. Next step for whoever picks this up: diff the exact JSON `/api/v1/topology`+`/api/v1/findings` payloads between a fresh daemon and a ~150s-old one, and check whether disabling the pulse/dash setInterval effects (or throttling the draw effect to rAF instead of per-mousemove viewport state) makes v2 alone-after-two-priors stop hanging.

entries.title: T-3406: axe sweep, every routed page, light and dark › axe: /audit (light)

Filed as a follow-up rather than fixed here because the pattern recurs across a large, page-local, pre-existing surface (this sweep alone found it on ~15 different pages, each its own component) that deserves a dedicated audit-and-fix task, not a scope expansion of this phase's close-out pass.
